brow: Aggregated snapshot · open-source compilation · not official reporting
editionNote: Morning edition. It covers the 24 hours to 05:10 CET on 26 October; new research covers 17:10 CET on 25 October to 05:10 CET on 26 October, items from the previous edition still inside the 24 hours were carried, and stories with new developments are marked as follow-ups.

theaters.heading: Battlefield, long-range strikes, and peace diplomacy in Russia's war on Ukraine

items.title: Jet Drones and Missiles Hit Ukraine's Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia Overnight
items.lede: Russia's raid was still under way at the cutoff, with at least two people injured, ballistic alerts over Kyiv, and the Air Force tally still pending.

sections.text: Russia attacked Ukraine with jet-powered Shahed-type drones through the night into 26 October, with the Air Force tracking groups from the north, from Bryansk region, and from the Black Sea toward Chornomorsk and Odesa region [1][2]. Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov reported a jet-drone hit in the city's Kholodnohirskyi district at 03:28 Kyiv time (02:28 CET) [1]. The Air Force warned of ballistic missiles at 03:33 Kyiv time, and media reported explosions in Kropyvnytskyi after missiles were tracked toward the city [1]. A strike on Zaporizhzhia damaged private houses, cars, and a commercial building, started a fire, and injured at least two people [1]. The Air Force tally for the night was not published by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate on the reported hits, because they rest on one live page relaying officials and the Air Force. The scale of the attack is not yet known.

items.title: Zelensky Offers to Spare Russian Refineries if Moscow Stops Hitting Ukraine's Grid
items.lede: Kyiv also said army limits and neutrality are off the table at the November talks, while energy, Black Sea grain, and prisoners are open.

sections.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told the TSN programme on 25 October that Ukraine would stop striking Russia's oil and diesel refining infrastructure if Russia stopped striking Ukraine's power grid, calling it a fair 'energy ceasefire' he had proposed to partners [3][4]. He said a trilateral meeting with US and Russian negotiating teams would take place in November, and that territory could only be discussed by leaders [5][4]. He listed energy, grain shipments in the Black Sea, and prisoner exchanges as the specifics he wanted on the table [5]. Zelensky said limits on Ukraine's army and neutrality were not up for discussion and that he would like to keep an 800,000-strong force [5][4]. He also said US warnings of imminent Russian ballistic missile strikes had been fully restored [4]. No Kremlin reply to the energy offer was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that Zelensky made these remarks, because three outlets report the interview consistently. The November date rests on statements by the two sides, not on an announced schedule.

items.title: Russian Drone Strike on a Kherson Minibus Kills a Ukrainian Passenger
items.lede: Six people aboard were hurt, and the city's military administration said a 67-year-old man later died in hospital.

sections.text: A Russian drone attacked a passenger minibus in Kherson, in southern Ukraine, at about 15:11 Kyiv time on 25 October (14:11 CET), injuring six people [6][7]. Yaroslav Shanko, head of the Kherson City Military Administration, said on Telegram that a 67-year-old man with severe injuries died in hospital despite resuscitation [7]. No Russian comment was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate, because the account rests on the city administration relayed by Ukraine's state news agency, without independent confirmation.

items.title: Russia's Belgorod Counts Three Dead and 30 Damaged Blocks After a Ukrainian Drone Swarm
items.lede: Russian officials later raised the city's death toll by one and reported another death in a separate daytime strike, while Kyiv made no claim.

sections.text: A large swarm of Ukrainian drones attacked the Russian city of Belgorod, near Ukraine's border, overnight into 25 October, and the regional headquarters confirmed a 'massive UAV attack' [8]. Russian authorities said on Sunday that two men were killed and 13 people injured in the city, AFP reported [9]. Mayor Valentin Demidov posted images of burning apartment blocks and cars and said homes and some social and commercial facilities were badly damaged [9]. The monitoring channel Exilenova Plus said the main target was the MegaGRINN shopping complex, the city's largest [8][10]. Acting Governor Aleksandr Shuvayev counted 154 attacks across the region in 24 hours, with two more men killed in the Shebekino and Graivoron districts [9]. On Sunday local authorities put the overnight toll in the city at three dead and 13 injured, said a separate drone strike later in the day killed another person, and Shuvayev said 30 apartment buildings were damaged, the Guardian reported [4]. No Ukrainian military claim for Belgorod city was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate on the toll, because Russian officials, a party to the war, are the only basis and counts differ between reports. Confidence on the target is low, because it rests on a monitoring channel.

items.title: Kremlin Aide Sets 4 November as the Earliest Date for Talks With Ukraine
items.lede: Yuri Ushakov called the first meeting a trial run and said Moscow, Beijing, and Washington were preparing a Putin, Trump, and Xi summit.

sections.text: Yuri Ushakov, Russian President Vladimir Putin's foreign policy aide, told state outlet Vesti on 25 October that Russia would be ready to resume trilateral talks with Ukraine and the US after 4 November, Russia's National Unity Day [11]. He called the first meeting after the pause a 'trial run' and said a peace agreement 'still needs work' [11][12]. Ushakov also said Moscow, Beijing, and Washington were 'in principle, ready' for a meeting of Putin, President Donald Trump, and Xi Jinping, and that preparations had begun [12]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on 23 October that a new round was expected in the first half of November, possibly in Abu Dhabi [11]. No White House or Chinese comment on a three-way summit was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that Ushakov made these remarks, because two outlets carry them from Russian state media. The three-way summit claim rests on the Kremlin alone.

items.title: Attacks Damage Industrial Sites in Russia's Perm Krai and Lipetsk Regions
items.lede: Russian governors confirmed six injured and damage at both sites, while monitoring channels named the Avisma and Energia defence suppliers, 1,400 and 200 kilometres from the border.

sections.text: Drones struck an industrial site in the north of Russia's Perm Krai on 25 October, causing minor damage and injuring five workers, Governor Dmitry Makhonin said, adding that 11 drones were downed [10][13]. The monitoring channel Exilenova Plus said the target was the Avisma titanium plant in Berezniki, more than 1,400 kilometres from Ukraine's border, part of VSMPO-Avisma and under US sanctions since 2023 [10][13]. Later the same day Lipetsk Governor Igor Artamonov said an industrial zone in Yelets was attacked, injuring one person [10][14]. Astra said the target was the Energia plant, which makes batteries for drones and air-defence missiles, and monitoring channels said cruise missiles were used [14][10]. Ukraine had not commented by the time of publication [10].

Confidence is high that both regions were attacked, because Russian governors confirmed it and two outlets report it. Confidence on the named plants is moderate, because they rest on monitoring channels and Astra.

items.title: Russia Launches 153 Drones at Ukraine Overnight, Hitting 15 Locations
items.lede: Air defences stopped 119 of them, but a strike in Vinnytsia wrecked four flats, injured six, and forced an evacuation of a nursing home.

sections.text: Russia attacked Ukraine with 153 strike drones from 18:00 Kyiv time on 24 October (17:00 CET), 92 of them jet-powered, launched from Bryansk, Oryol, Kursk, Millerovo, occupied Donetsk, and Crimea, the Air Force said [15][16]. By 08:00 Kyiv time defences had downed or suppressed 119, with hits at 15 locations and debris at nine [15][16]. In Vinnytsia a drone hit a five-storey building, destroying four apartments and injuring six people, and damaged a private nursing home from which 15 residents were evacuated, Governor Nataliia Zabolotna said [17][16]. Local authorities counted eight dead and 51 injured across Ukraine over the past day [16]. The Epicenter retail chain said its hypermarkets in Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Vinnytsia, and Poltava were struck within a day [18].
Confidence is high on the launch figures and the Vinnytsia damage, because the Air Force and the governor are on record and two outlets agree. The Epicenter claim rests on the company's own post.

items.title: Blackout Hits Occupied Crimea After a Strike on Russia's Taman Substation
items.lede: The Russian-installed Sevastopol governor confirmed the outage, and power briefly returned before new cuts hit several cities and internet monitors logged wide disruption.

sections.text: A blackout hit Russian-occupied Crimea in Ukraine overnight into 24 October after an attack on energy infrastructure, with outages in Sevastopol, Simferopol, Yalta, Feodosia, and other towns [19][20]. NASA FIRMS satellite data showed damage at the Taman substation in Russia's Krasnodar region, the peninsula's link to the Russian grid [20]. Sevastopol's Russian-installed governor Mikhail Razvozhayev confirmed the outage, saying social facilities switched to backup power [19][20]. Power later returned in several cities, but residents reported new outages in Simferopol, Yalta, and Alushta [20]. Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov restricted electricity and water supplies, blaming a Ukrainian attack [21], and Russia's Energy Ministry said parts of occupied Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, Donetsk, and Luhansk regions also lost power [22]. Late on 24 October Razvozhayev said only about 40 percent of Sevastopol's apartment buildings had power [23]. On 25 October he said power reached almost all homes by morning, but the grid overloaded again about an hour later, and from 12:00 Sevastopol moved to rolling '3 through 3' outages to protect supply to homes [24][25]. NetBlocks reported wide internet outages [20]. No Ukrainian military claim for the Taman strike was found.
Confidence is high that a wide outage occurred, because the Russian-installed governor confirmed it; it is moderate on the cause, which rests on monitoring channels and satellite fire data.

items.title: Russian Drone Kills Three in an Apartment Block in Ukraine's Synelnykove
items.lede: By Sunday morning 14 people were counted injured, five of them in serious condition, while further drones killed one person in Kharkiv and hit central Kyiv.

sections.text: A Russian drone struck a high-rise in Synelnykove, in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, on the evening of 24 October, setting the fourth floor on fire and destroying a store and several cars, Governor Oleksandr Hanzha said [26][27]. Three people were killed [26][27]. Hanzha first reported at least eight injured, including an 11-year-old girl, and later at least 12, with two in serious condition undergoing surgery [26][27]. Later that night a jet-powered drone hit Kharkiv's Novobavarskyi district, killing one person and injuring four, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said [28]. Drone debris fell on a car park in central Kyiv, damaging cars and injuring one person, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said [29]. A strike on an energy facility cut power to one district of Vinnytsia region, with no injuries, its governor said [30]. On the morning of 25 October Hanzha put the Synelnykove district toll at three dead and 14 injured, five of them hospitalised in serious condition [16].

Confidence is high on the Synelnykove deaths, because the governor is on record in two outlets; the injury count rose between reports. Confidence on the Kharkiv, Kyiv, and Vinnytsia details is moderate, because only Ukrinform was read.

items.title: Drones Reach Siberia's Omsk, 2,500 Kilometres From Ukraine, and Hit a Logistics Hub
items.lede: Omsk's governor confirmed a logistics hub was struck and staff evacuated, while a Ukrainian monitoring channel also reported a fire at a petrochemical plant tied to missile fuel.

sections.text: Drones attacked the Russian city of Omsk in Siberia, about 2,500 kilometres from Ukraine, on 24 October, Governor Vitaly Khotsenko said, adding that a logistics hub was hit, staff were evacuated, and emergency services were at the scene [31][32]. The Ukrainian monitoring channel Exilenova Plus said a fire broke out at the Omsky Kauchuk petrochemical plant, a maker of synthetic rubber that it tied to Iskander rocket fuel supply, and that a warehouse of online retailer Ozon was also hit [31]. Ozon confirmed its Omsk logistics centre was hit, saying all staff were evacuated, no one was hurt according to preliminary information, and a fire broke out [33]. The Kyiv Independent said it could not verify the reports [31]. On 25 October Khotsenko said three people were injured in the attack, which lasted six hours [34]. Russia's Defence Ministry listed Omsk region among areas where it said 125 Ukrainian drones were downed on 24 October, without a separate count for Omsk; no Ukrainian General Staff claim was found [35].

Confidence is high that drones struck Omsk and hit Ozon's logistics centre, because the governor and the company confirmed it; confidence on the plant fire is low, because it rests on a monitoring channel without Russian official confirmation.

items.title: French Navy Patrol Plane Flies From Romania to Guard Black Sea Shipping
items.lede: Paris says the NATO-tasked Atlantique 2 helped rescue crews from attacked merchant ships, while a US P-8A Poseidon has also patrolled off Bulgaria.

sections.text: A French Navy Atlantique 2 maritime patrol aircraft has been operating over the western Black Sea from Constanța, Romania, after a run of drone attacks on merchant ships off Romania and Bulgaria [1][2]. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said in Varna, Bulgaria, on 24 October that the NATO-tasked plane had been in the region for two weeks and had helped in rescues, noting three ships attacked, one of which sank within minutes about 100 kilometres from Varna [2][1]. Flight-tracking data cited by the Romanian outlet Curs de Guvernare put its arrival in Constanța on 18 October, Militarnyi reported on 25 October [1]. A US Navy P-8A Poseidon from Sigonella in Sicily also patrolled near Bulgaria's coast [1]. NATO agreed on 20 October to step up Black Sea surveillance [1][2].
Confidence is high on the deployment, because the French minister confirmed it on record and two outlets report it. The arrival date rests on flight-tracking data relayed by one outlet.

items.title: Poland Says It Knows Which GRU Unit Runs Russia's Hybrid Attacks in Europe
items.lede: Radosław Sikorski did not name the military intelligence unit or show evidence, but warned that Moscow is planning escalation beyond daily cyberattacks and sabotage.

sections.text: Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski told CNN's Fareed Zakaria in an interview published on 25 October that Russia is waging a hybrid war against Europe, citing attacks in Poland, the UK, and Germany, arson, and a failed attempt to derail a train [3][4]. 'We know which specific GRU unit is behind this, and we know they are planning escalation,' he said, according to PAP [3][4]. He said Poland faces daily cyberattacks on hospitals and the financial and energy systems, plus drone incursions, espionage, and mapping of critical maritime infrastructure [3]. Sikorski did not name the unit or describe the evidence or the planned escalation [4]. He said more aid to Ukraine was the best answer to Russian provocations [3]. No Russian response was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high that Sikorski made the statement, because two outlets carry the same quote from PAP. Confidence is low on the attribution itself, because Warsaw has published no evidence.

items.title: Sanctioned Russian Shadow-Fleet Tanker Sends Distress Call West of Ireland
items.lede: The UK Coastguard sent an RAF patrol plane to the ship, which then sailed on after avoiding the English Channel on its way from Ust-Luga.

sections.text: The oil products tanker Myra, sanctioned by the US, the EU, the UK, Canada, Switzerland, and Ukraine, sent an Inmarsat-C distress signal on 24 October about 188 nautical miles west of Ireland, the monitoring project SeaNews reported [5][6]. The Insider gave the time as 12:38 UTC (13:38 CET), while the Navy Lookout account cited by UNITED24 said around midnight [5][6]. The UK Coastguard coordinated the response and a Royal Air Force P-8A Poseidon made contact with the 21 people aboard, who said the alarm was raised while leaving rough seas, and the ship continued its voyage [6]. The tanker had sailed from Russia's Baltic port of Ust-Luga around the north of Scotland, avoiding the English Channel, a route other shadow-fleet ships use [5][6]. The IMO lists its Cameroon flag as false, and Ukrainian intelligence links it to a network run by the son of Iran's Ali Shamkhani [5]. No damage or leak was reported by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate on the distress call and response, because two outlets agree but both rely on monitoring projects and secondary accounts. The ownership links rest on Ukrainian intelligence, a party to the war.

items.title: Russia Claims Drone Strikes on Two Cargo Ships Bound for Ukraine's Ports
items.lede: Moscow added a second vessel heading for Odesa to its claims, but named neither ship and gave no damage details, and Reuters could not verify either.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Russia's Defence Ministry said its drones struck a cargo ship heading for Ukraine's Black Sea port of Chornomorsk overnight into 25 October, claiming the vessel was supplying Ukraine's armed forces, Reuters reported via Digi24 [7]. The ministry gave no name for the ship and no details of damage [7]. It also claimed strikes on three logistics sites in Kharkiv that it said stored dual-use goods [7]. Reuters said it could not verify the claims [7]. Later on Sunday the ministry said its drones had also struck a second cargo vessel en route to the port of Odesa during the day, again saying the ships supplied Ukraine's army; Reuters could not confirm it, the Guardian reported [8]. No Ukrainian confirmation of a ship being hit was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is low on the strike itself, because it rests on Russia's Defence Ministry, a party to the war, relayed by one outlet and not independently verified.

items.title: Romania's Defence Minister Makes Counter-Drone Defence a Top Priority
items.lede: Radu Oprea said F-16 pilots from Borcea had downed five drones this year, including two recently over the Black Sea, while Spanish jets downed a sixth.

sections.text: Romanian Defence Minister Radu Oprea told troops at the 86th Air Base at Borcea on 25 October, Romania's Army Day, that building capabilities to detect and counter drone threats and making the Black Sea security hub operational were among his priorities [9][10]. He said Romanian F-16 pilots from Borcea had recently shot down two attack drones over the Black Sea after they entered Romanian airspace [9][10]. Oprea said Borcea pilots had downed five drones this year, Spanish F-18 pilots a sixth, and Borcea pilots another in allied airspace, according to a Defence Ministry statement [10]. Chief of Defence Staff General Gheorghiță Vlad said the shoot-downs showed Romania's army could answer real threats [10]. Oprea named no dates, drone types, or locations for the individual interceptions [10].

Confidence is high that the minister made these statements, because the state news agency and a defence outlet quoting a ministry statement agree. The interception tally rests on Romania's Defence Ministry alone.

items.title: Thousands Rally in Prague Against Czech Plan to Scrap Public-Media Licence Fees
items.lede: Broadcaster employees plan an all-day strike on 3 Nov, and organisers called another rally on Letná Plain for 15 Nov after the overnight first-reading vote.

sections.text: Thousands of people filled Prague's Old Town Square in the Czech Republic on Sunday to protest a coalition bill replacing Czech Television and Czech Radio licence fees with state funding, and police closed access from surrounding streets, ČTK reported [1][2]. The lower house passed the bill in first reading at 04:36 on Saturday; it would cut the broadcasters' funding by about CZK 1.4 billion and now goes to committee [1][2]. Mikuláš Minář, head of the organisers Milion chvilek pro demokracii, called on Prime Minister Andrej Babiš and coalition partners Tomio Okamura and Petr Macinka to withdraw it and join a public debate [1]. Critics warn that state funding could expose the broadcasters to political pressure [2]. ČTK judged the crowd markedly larger than at the group's 28 Sep protest [1]. No response from Babiš was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the protest, the vote, and the organisers' demands, because ČTK via Czech Television and Expats.cz report them; the funding cut and the strike plan rest on Expats.cz, and no crowd estimate was published.

items.title: Le Pen Opens French Presidential Bid Promising a Bardella-Led Unity Government
items.lede: The National Rally leader, ahead in every poll for next May's election, also vowed to write the 'national community' into the Constitution and keep young people out of foreign wars.

sections.text: France's far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen launched her presidential campaign on Sunday at the party's congress in Orléans, promising a "national unity" and "pluralist" government led by party president Jordan Bardella if she wins next May, AFP reported [3][4]. "The state we want will not be RN" but a patriotic, non-partisan collective work, she said [3][4]. She said she would write "the national community" into the Constitution and recognise only one people, and pledged that France would not send young people to die in wars "that are not ours" [3]. During Bardella's earlier speech, party stewards removed several people from the hall, including Union of Jewish Students of France activists who unfurled a banner; the group said they were removed very violently [3]. The congress was held under heavy security, with protests banned in the city [3]. No government reaction was found by the cutoff.
Confidence is high on Le Pen's pledges, because AFP reports them via 20 Minutes and La Libre; the account of the stewards' force rests on the student group's statement.

items.title: Italy's Salvini Vows to Press Cabinet to Halt Money and Weapons for Ukraine
items.lede: League delegates in Milan gave the deputy prime minister 465 votes to Massimo Garavaglia's 146, keeping him at the party's helm until 2030.

sections.text: Italy's deputy prime minister Matteo Salvini was confirmed as secretary of the League (Lega) on Sunday with 465 votes, 76% of the 611 valid ballots, against 146 for challenger Massimo Garavaglia, at the party's extraordinary congress in Milan, La Stampa and ANSA reported [5][6][7]. Only eight ballots were blank or spoiled, and Salvini will lead the party until 2030 [5][7]. Before the vote, Salvini said that if confirmed he would tell the Council of Ministers to stop money and arms for Ukraine, adding that he would go with this clear position [8]. Salvini said the League would win the next elections with Giorgia Meloni and be the coalition's second party [5]. The head of Italy's journalists' association, Carlo Bartoli, likened Salvini's attack on journalists in his victory speech to Russia and China [5]. La Repubblica reported early on Monday that Meloni called Salvini to tell him 'Così mi metti in difficoltà' ('you're putting me in a difficult position') [9]; no defence ministry response was found.

Confidence is high on the vote and Salvini's statements, because La Stampa and ANSA report them on record; Meloni's call rests on La Repubblica alone; whether the cabinet changes Italy's Ukraine policy is not reported.

items.title: Brussels Police Defend Confiscating Goggles and Saline From Belgian Protesters
items.lede: Officers took swimming and ski goggles and face masks from people heading to Saturday's march, and their commander says the items were seized as a preventive measure.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Brussels police said on Sunday that officers acted lawfully when they "preventively" confiscated saline vials, protective, swimming, and ski goggles, and face masks from people about to join Saturday's protest in central Brussels, Belgium, Belga reported [10]. Several hundred people had gathered at the Mont des Arts before the march, at the call of groups including the Front des Mères and École en Lutte [11]. Commissioner Linda Camarero-Verde of the Brussels-Capital-Ixelles police zone acknowledged that carrying such items is not banned but said the march was tolerated only on condition that no irregularities occurred, calling the measures specific to its context [10]. Brussels police said about 400 people took part; five were detained for disturbing public order and four arrested over prohibited weapons and incitement to violence [12][13]. Belgian Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said on X that the protests ended without major incident, thanked police for their firmness, and said those behind damage and fires must be identified and punished [12]. No complaint or court challenge was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate on the police statement, because only Belga via La Libre reports it so far; confidence is high on Saturday's arrest figures, because Belga, RTBF, La Libre, and Reuters report them.

items.title: Milan Prosecutors Detain Alleged Mastermind of Italy's Movimento 17 Ottobre
items.lede: Youssef Siher, a 30-year-old researcher, faces suspected incitement with terrorist aims and organised protest violence under the new decree, and his wife is also under investigation.

sections.text: Italian police on Saturday night detained Youssef Siher, a 30-year-old Italian researcher considered the mastermind of the Movimento 17 ottobre linked to last weekend's clashes in central Milan, on the order of Milan prosecutors, ANSA reported [14]. He is suspected of incitement to commit crimes aggravated by terrorist aims and of organised violence at public demonstrations under Article 420 bis of the new decree [14]. His wife is under investigation without arrest for the same offences [14]. Earlier he had been questioned at Milan police headquarters while a home was searched, Corriere della Sera reported, citing Tg1 [15]. The 500 Folgore paratroopers sent under the decree patrolled central Milan alongside police [15][16]. On Sunday ANSA reported that only Siher and his wife administered the movement's chats, which had about 100,000 followers on Telegram and almost 50,000 on Instagram [17]. On Sunday evening Milan prosecutors said Siher had created a state of intimidation among the population through the movement, an element they cite for the terrorism aggravating factor, ANSA reported [18].

Confidence is high on the detention and the charges, because ANSA reports the prosecutors' order; the earlier questioning rests on Corriere citing Tg1, and the chat-administrator and intimidation details rest on ANSA summaries only.

items.title: Storm Boelo Kills Two Men in Britain and Cuts Power to 90,000 Properties
items.lede: Falling trees struck the victims in north London and southwest Scotland, while the stricken freighter off the Dutch coast got under way again on reduced engine power.
items.flag: FOLLOW UP TO PREVIOUS REPORT · single-source, unconfirmed

sections.text: Two men were killed by falling trees in the UK on Sunday during Storm Boelo: a man in his 20s whose car was hit in Finchley, north London, at about 13:40 CET, and a 60-year-old near Castle Douglas in Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland, police said, the BBC reported [19]. More than 90,000 properties were without power at 20:00 CET, the Energy Networks Association said, and 838,700 lost power during Storms Austen and Boelo [19]. Gusts peaked on Sunday morning at 85mph in Machrihanish, in Argyll and Bute, the BBC reported [19]. In the Netherlands on Sunday, Schiphol cancelled nearly 80 flights until 17:00 because not all runways could be used in the wind, and fallen trees halted trains between Lochem and Goor [20]. The 150-metre Portuguese-flagged freighter UHL Freedom, which lost anchor grip north of Schiermonnikoog, sailed on under its own limited power from 18:35 CET, the Dutch coastguard said; NOS now reports three of its 25 crew injured, down from five [21][22].

Confidence is high on the deaths, the power cuts, and the Dutch incidents, because the BBC and NOS attribute them to police, the Energy Networks Association, Schiphol, and the Dutch coastguard; each country rests on one outlet, and the crew injury count changed.

items.title: French Prosecutors Probe Far-Right Attacks on Nice Marchers as Arrests Reach 1,314
items.lede: High-school groups will meet the prime minister on Monday, and a prosecutor said a police grenade may have caused a protester's serious hand injury.

sections.text: France's interior ministry said on Sunday that police made 1,314 arrests during Saturday's nationwide protests and that 53 police officers and gendarmes were injured [23][24]. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez had said on Saturday evening that the marches went smoothly, while acknowledging 'a great many' incidents of violence, and the ministry's Sunday figure replaced his initial estimate of nearly a thousand [23]. Paris police reported 142 arrests and 126 people in custody [23]. In Nice, prosecutor Damien Martinelli opened an aggravated-violence investigation into attacks on marchers; 11 of the 59 people detained may belong to the far right, and masks, gas sprays, and batons were found in vehicles [3][25]. Nuñez said far-right militants sought clashes with the far left in at least Nice and Montpellier; LFI's Mathilde Panot counted 14 cities [3]. In Clermont-Ferrand, prosecutor Eric Serfass opened an inquiry into a protester's serious hand injury, possibly from a police grenade [3]. High-school groups told AFP the prime minister will receive them on Monday at 14:30; they want Parcoursup scrapped [3]. The Yellow Vests have called further protests for 31 Oct [24].
Confidence is high on the national, Paris, and Nice figures, because officials spoke on record and four outlets report them; the grenade link is the prosecutor's preliminary view.

items.title: Barcelona Police Arrest 128 After Looting and Fires in Spain's Catalan Capital
items.lede: Seventy-two of those held were minors, four officers were seriously hurt, and police are now investigating who organised the social-media calls behind Saturday's unrest.

sections.text: Spain's Catalan police, the Mossos d'Esquadra, and Barcelona's city police arrested 128 people after unauthorised protests called on social media around Plaça de Catalunya on Saturday turned violent, the city council said on Sunday [26][27]. About two hours after the 16:00 local time (15:00 CET) deployment of 524 officers, hooded groups threw objects at police, burned bins, and looted and vandalised shops until about 22:00 local time (21:00 CET) [26]. Of those held, 122 are men and six women, 72 are minors, and only two had previous public-order records [26][27]. The council counted 14 officers hurt, four seriously, 23 shops vandalised, 31 bins burned, and 33 fire-brigade call-outs; EFE, citing police, reported 15 officers hurt [26][27]. Police seized knives, sprays, balaclavas, fireworks, and stones and opened 68 administrative reports [26]. An investigation targets those who organised the online calls, and the mayor ordered immediate legal action over damage to city property [26]. Spanish media said the calls echoed the French protests, and Catalan regional president Salvador Illa condemned the violence, NOS reported [28].

Confidence is high on the arrests, injuries, and damage, because the Barcelona city council and police published them and EFE and NOS report them; the injured-officer count differs by one between sources.

items.title: Kulbergs Delays Latvia's Coalition Talks, Leaving Partners Without a Program
items.lede: Formal talks on the next government are now due to start on Wednesday, 28 October, with the National Alliance first in line.

sections.text: Nearly all of October has passed in Latvia without formal party consultations on the next government, and neither politicians nor the public have seen Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs's promised change plan, coalition model, or ministers, LTV's De facto reported [1]. Kulbergs, whose United List holds 41 seats, postponed the plan's presentation after travelling to a friend's funeral in the United States, and says formal talks will begin on Wednesday [1]. The National Alliance will go first, and many of its members want Interior Minister Jānis Dombrava to keep his post [1]. New Unity also has an invitation and said it would not back golden-visa schemes [1]. Latvia First leader Ainārs Šlesers again offered a United List coalition with 58 votes or support for a minority government without posts [1].
Confidence is moderate, because the account rests on one LTV programme; the timetable and positions are the politicians' own statements to it.

items.title: Latvian Prosecutor Says Belarusian Guards Send Indebted Migrants to Sabotage the Border
items.lede: Latvia has logged more than 60 cases of damaged border infrastructure this year, against 23 in all of 2025, as the Belarus-backed migration route strains.

sections.text: A Latvian prosecutor told LTV's De facto programme that uniformed officials visit migrant camps on the Belarusian side, check whether people have paid for an illegal crossing, and send those who have not to damage Latvia's border infrastructure, with beatings or torture if they refuse [2]. Andris Aleksejevs of the Prosecutor General's Office said a criminal case opened in July rests on reasonable suspicion that Belarusian border guard officials are involved in organising illegal migration and damaging Latvian infrastructure [2]. Border guard data show more than 60 cases of damage this year, including electrical cabinets and cameras, against 23 last year, and more than 12,000 illegal crossing attempts have been prevented in 2026 [2]. Smugglers on the Belarusian side threw stones at border guards at least twice last week, De facto reported [2]. A Telegram group calling itself the Black Russians claimed one sabotage episode in early October [2]. No Belarusian response was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate: the account rests on one LTV report quoting Latvian prosecutors, border guards, and the military; the claims about Belarusian officials are allegations in an open criminal case.

items.title: Estonia Plans to Ship Locomotives to Ukraine to Replace Rolling Stock Russia Destroyed
items.lede: Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said Russian strikes have destroyed or damaged 340 railway carriages this year and that Kyiv needs more extensive practical help this winter.

sections.text: Estonia is planning to send a substantial number of locomotives to Ukraine to help keep its transport links running, Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna told ERR News [3]. Tsahkna said he discussed Russia's attacks and winter assistance with Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha by telephone last week [3]. He said Russia has targeted the transport network and has already destroyed or damaged 340 railway carriages this year [3]. ERR did not report a number of locomotives or a delivery date.
Confidence is moderate, because the plan rests on Tsahkna's remarks reported by ERR alone; the carriage figure is his and was not independently checked.

items.title: Estonian Defense Minister Wants About a Dozen Light Jets to Hunt Attack Drones
items.lede: Martin Herem said a purchase could take up to four years; the three Baltic air forces have no fighters of their own and rely on NATO's air policing mission.

sections.text: Estonia could need around a dozen light fighter jets to counter jet-powered attack drones, and procurement could take up to four years, Defense Minister Martin Herem told ERR News [4]. Herem said Ukraine uses F-16s to destroy nearly half of such drones but that Estonia could not afford that route, so smaller jet aircraft are being considered [4]. ERR said fighter jets cost between €15 million and €100 million each, and that Estonia's air force has used two Czech L-39 jets for training for 15 years [4].
Confidence is moderate, because the account rests on one ERR report of the minister's own remarks; no procurement decision has been announced.

items.title: Serbia's Student List Wins a Parliamentary Majority as Vučić Concedes Defeat
items.lede: Ipsos and CeSID project 140 of 250 seats for the movement on a record turnout near 70 percent, and EU leaders pledged support for reforms.

sections.text: Serbia's opposition Student List won the 25 October snap parliamentary election, in which 18 lists were on the ballot [1], according to Ipsos and CeSID projections, which at 96 percent of the sample gave it 52.9 percent and 140 of 250 seats, against 38.8 percent and 103 seats for Aleksandar Vučić's United Serbia, with four other lists sharing seven [2]. The Guardian put the updated projection at 141 seats, against 126 needed for a majority, and turnout just below 70 percent, the highest since 1990 [3]. These are projections, not election commission (RIK) results [2]. At about 21:30, Vučić said that, based on the stratified sample, his list had clearly lost [4] [5], and he called the result the verification of a revolution backed by European countries and the US deep state [5]. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa said they stood ready to support reforms and Serbia's path to the EU, and Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos said the door to the EU was open [3]. Serbia must also elect a new president, since Vučić stepped down to run [3].
Confidence is high on the outcome, which rests on the projections, Vučić's concession, and several outlets; seat totals are projections and may shift slightly in official counts.

items.title: Bulgaria's Yotova and Gyurov Head for a 1 November Presidential Run-Off
items.lede: Official partial results give the Radev-backed incumbent a lead of about three points over the pro-Western former caretaker premier, on turnout near 22 percent.

sections.text: With 84.57 percent of polling-station protocols processed, Bulgaria's Central Election Commission had incumbent President Iliana Yotova and Kiril Valchev on 34.62 percent and Andrey Gyurov and Georgi Kandev on 31.91 percent, followed by Revival leader Kostadin Kostadinov and Petar Volgin on 12.66 percent, BNT reported [6]. Because no ticket won a majority, the top two go to a run-off on 1 November [6] [7]. Yotova is backed by Prime Minister Rumen Radev's Progressive Bulgaria and favours dialogue with Moscow, while Gyurov is backed by pro-Western opposition parties; pre-election polls had put her between 41 and 47 percent [7]. Pollsters estimated turnout at about 22 percent [8]. Interior Minister Ivan Demerdzhiev called polling day calm and said no serious attempts at vote buying or manipulation had been identified [8]. Earlier in the day the commission had replaced 20 failed voting machines with paper ballots [9]. Euronews said preliminary results were expected on Monday [7].
Confidence is high on the run-off pairing and the partial commission figures, which BNT, Euronews, and the pollsters agree on; final shares may change as counting ends.

items.title: Albanian Police Detain Protesters at Rama's Office as Unrest Enters a 13th Day
items.lede: Police had already arrested 23 people and declared 30 wanted over Saturday's clashes in Tirana, while Prime Minister Edi Rama said violence cannot force him out.

sections.text: On the evening of 25 October, the 13th day of student-led protests in Tirana, Albania, police began taking some protesters into custody outside Prime Minister Edi Rama's office after trying to disperse the gathering, Albeu reported at 19:00; no official tally was released [10]. Earlier, protesters threw stones at the Ministry of Education before marching on his office [11]. State Police said on Sunday morning that they had arrested 23 people, opened criminal proceedings against 13 more, and declared 30 wanted after Saturday's protest, when officers were attacked with stones, Molotov cocktails, and gas canisters rigged with detonators [12]. Rama, presenting a package of laws against urban violence, said his resignation could not be imposed through violence and promised 2027 budget measures early this week, the state agency ATA reported [13]. On 24 October police used water cannon and tear gas at the ministry [14] [15], and the Health Ministry said 13 people, including two journalists, were hurt [16]. The Health Ministry had put injuries since the protests began at 310, including 191 police officers, on 19 October [17].
Confidence is high on the police arrest figures and Rama's remarks; the Sunday evening detentions rest on Albeu alone, with no police count by the cutoff.

items.title: Bosnia's Election Commission Certifies Results, Making Minić Republika Srpska President
items.lede: SNSD leader Milorad Dodik said Republika Srpska's assembly would sit by 20 November and that a new government and budget would follow by late December.

sections.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina's Central Election Commission certified the results of the 4 October general elections at an urgent session on the evening of 24 October, confirming Savo Minić of the SNSD as president of Republika Srpska and giving the SNSD 34 of the entity assembly's 83 seats [18]. Certification opens a 72-hour window for recount requests and objections, with appeals to the Court of BiH, and the results become final only after those deadlines pass [18]. In Banja Luka on 25 October, Dodik said the assembly's constitutive session would be held by 20 November, where the president would take the oath, if final results were confirmed by 4 November [19]. He said the SNSD did not intend to form a coalition with anyone and would keep its partnership with the HDZ, which he said was not aimed at Bosniaks [19]. No statement from the Office of the High Representative was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is moderate: the certification and seat figures rest on one detailed Srpske Novine report of the commission's decision, while Dodik's timetable is reported by both Srna via Nezavisne novine and Srpske Novine.

items.title: Armenia's Ruling Civil Contract Wins Most of 21 Local Races
items.lede: The opposition Solidarity alliance took Goris and Gavar, and observers reported breaches of ballot secrecy after a wave of pre-vote arrests of opposition candidates.

sections.text: Armenia's Minister of Territorial Administration, David Khudatyan, published preliminary results for 17 of the 21 communities that voted on 25 October, showing Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's Civil Contract ahead in most, Caucasian Knot reported [1]. Civil Contract's highest shares were 96.12 percent in Vayk, 96.1 percent in Armavir, and 94.2 percent in Garni, while it took 74.9 percent in Artik and 47.8 percent in Yeghegnadzor [1] [2]. The Solidarity alliance won 93 percent in Goris and 81.3 percent in Gavar [1]. Observers reported violations of ballot secrecy, procedural breaches, and illegal control, and the opposition said many Armenians working abroad could not vote [1]. Before the vote, police detained 24 people in Stepanavan, including Strong Armenia candidate Arsen Gevorgyan, who was later arrested [1]. By 17:00 local time turnout had ranged up to 58.36 percent in Stepanavan [3]. No certified election commission results were found by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: the results are a minister's preliminary figures relayed by Caucasian Knot and NEWS.am, which agree; they are not certified, and the violation reports are observers' claims.

items.title: Georgia's Opposition Launches a 'Georgia Without Ivanishvili' Protest Wave
items.lede: Thousands marched to Rustaveli Avenue as Georgian Dream seeks a court ban on opposition parties, and leaders set 28 November as the next big rally.

sections.text: Opposition parties and civil society groups in Georgia marched from Tbilisi State University toward Rustaveli Avenue on 25 October under the slogan "Georgia without Ivanishvili", which organisers called the start of a new wave of protests, Caucasian Knot reported [4]. Citing Publika video, it said thousands took part, carrying Georgian, Ukrainian, and EU flags, with a large police presence [4]. The march came as the Constitutional Court considers Georgian Dream's lawsuit to ban opposition parties [4]. Coalition for Change leader Nika Gvaramia said the movement needed a culmination on 28 November, two years after protests began [4] [5]. European Georgia leader Gigi Tsereteli said parties were being banned and political life restricted [5]. Genews reported that the rally ended at about 22:37 local time (19:37 CET) [5]. The previous evening's weekly march drew hundreds [6]. No detentions were reported for Sunday's march by the cutoff.
Confidence is moderate: two outlets agree on the march and the speeches, but the crowd size rests on Publika video cited by Caucasian Knot, and no police figure was found.

items.title: Two SPD Ministers Unveil a Bill Letting Builders Skip Costly Comfort Standards
items.lede: Germany's ministries expect simpler homes to cut building costs by 10 to 15 percent, though the CDU wanted no separate contract type.

sections.text: German Justice Minister Stefanie Hubig and Construction Minister Verena Hubertz (both SPD) present a draft 'Gebäudetyp E' law on Monday that would let parties to a building contract agree to waive non-mandatory comfort standards [1] [2]. Examples include thinner ceilings, fewer sockets, lower ceiling heights, and unheated stairwells; fire safety, structural safety, ventilation, and light are excluded [1]. Ministries expect building costs to fall by 10 to 15 percent, citing pilot projects [1]. The draft, seen by ARD, makes the option a separate voluntary contract category, a point CDU housing spokesman Jan-Marco Luczak had opposed, arguing it could create two-class building [2]. The bill now goes to the federal states and industry associations for comment, and is not yet agreed within the government [2] [1]. The ministers aim for it to take effect in mid-2027 at the earliest [1].

Confidence is high on the draft's content and timing, because ARD has seen it and dpa reports the ministers' own statements. Confidence is moderate on the savings estimate, which rests on the ministries' reading of pilot projects.

items.title: Storm Gust Drives a Cruise Ship Into Freighters in Germany's Bremerhaven
items.lede: No one was hurt, but crushed lifeboats kept the 2,428-guest Mein Schiff 3 in port as forecasters expected a storm surge in Hamburg overnight.

sections.text: Storm Luise left damage mainly in western and southwestern Germany on Friday, seriously injuring two people in Nastätten, Rhineland-Palatinate [3] [4]. On Sunday, storm Manja brought gale warnings to much of Germany, with 135 km/h measured on the Brocken [5]; in Freiburg, a gust cut power for some 25,000 people until midday [6]. In Bremerhaven, TUI Cruises' Mein Schiff 3 collided while leaving port on Sunday evening; police later said three ships were involved [7]. A heavy gust pushed the ship against the freighter MSC Victorine around 17:00, crushing several lifeboats and tenders, and authorities barred the onward voyage to the Canary Islands [8]. The container ship has a tear about 10 meters long, but there was no water ingress; 2,428 guests and 922 crew were aboard, and the water police are investigating the cause [7]. The federal maritime agency forecast a storm surge overnight, with water about 4.10 meters above sea-level datum at Hamburg's St. Pauli gauge around 04:00 Monday; ferries to the Halligen are cancelled on Monday [9].

Confidence is high on the collision, the ships, the people aboard, and the damage, because tagesschau and Merkur cite police, port authorities, and TUI Cruises. Confidence is moderate on the gust as cause and on surge levels, which rest on early reports and forecasts.

items.title: Germany's Audi Commits About $4 Billion to Its First US Factory
items.lede: Trump unveiled the plant at a campaign rally about a week before the 3 November midterms, with Audi's chief on stage beside him.

sections.text: German carmaker Audi, a Volkswagen subsidiary, said it plans its first U.S. production site in Georgia, investing around $4 billion and creating about 4,500 jobs [10]. The plant is designed for up to 200,000 vehicles a year, mainly premium SUVs, with construction from 2027 and production from the early 2030s [10] [11]. President Donald Trump announced the project at a Republican campaign event in Georgia on Saturday, putting it at $4.2 billion and saying construction would start next month [11]. Audi chief Gernot Döllner joined him on stage, saying he believes in the American market; the Stuttgarter Zeitung ran a separate commentary calling the appearance an embarrassing service to Trump's campaign [11]. SPD Bundestag member Isabel Cademartori called Döllner's appearance 'a disgrace, especially in light of the history of the VW group' and campaign help for an autocrat, while Lower Saxony premier Olaf Lies, who sits on VW's supervisory board, said the board must decide on an investment of this size [12]. Döllner said on Sunday that 'if the American president invites you, you accept the invitation' [13]. No federal government statement was found.
Confidence is high on the plan, investment, jobs, and timeline, because Audi's release states them and dpa confirms them. Trump's higher figure and earlier start date conflict with Audi's account.

items.title: Germany's Söder Presses for a November Deal on Aigner as Merz Stays Silent
items.lede: The CDU will not take up the presidency question until 9 November, deputy leader Michael Kretschmer said, while an SPD state leader called Aigner very suitable.

sections.text: Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) closed the CSU party congress in Munich, Germany, on Saturday but said nothing about the CSU's push for Bavarian Landtag President Ilse Aigner as federal president, though mentioning her at the start of his speech set off a storm of cheering among delegates, most of whom rose from their seats [14] [15]. CDU women want one of their own, and the CDU claims the nomination [16] [17]. Merz said anyone thinking of voting AfD 'has no place in our Union' [15]. On Sunday SPD chief whip Dirk Wiese and Greens parliamentary leader Britta Haßelmann said the office should go to a woman [18]. On ARD on Sunday evening, Söder said a decision would best come 'now in November' and that the CSU had held neither the chancellery nor the presidency in 75 years [19] [16]. Saxony's premier and CDU deputy leader Michael Kretschmer called Aigner excellent but not the only suitable candidate, saying the CDU would discuss it on 9 November [19]. Bremen's SPD mayor Andreas Bovenschulte called her very suitable, saying the CDU and Merz must now decide [19].
Confidence is high on the quoted remarks, reported by tagesschau, dpa, and n-tv, and moderate on the CDU position, which rests partly on unnamed party circles.

items.title: Germany's Dobrindt Drafts Law to Block Berlin's Plan to Socialise Housing Firms
items.lede: The federal plan would demand market-value cash compensation, undercutting the 16-billion-euro budget Berlin's SPD, Greens, and Left have set for buying out big landlords.

sections.text: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU) is preparing an investment protection law that would set high hurdles for socialising private housing, telling Bild that 'arbitrary left-wing socialisation fetish' is incompatible with the Basic Law [20] [21]; his ministry confirmed the details [21]. Under the key points, a state government would have to prove compelling necessity and that it had exhausted all other means, such as funding housing construction, and compensation would have to be paid in money at market value set by an expert appraisal [20]. The SPD, Greens, and Left in Berlin plan in their exploratory paper to act against landlords with more than 10,000 flats, budgeting 16 billion euros in compensation, below market value, with a bill due in mid-2028 [20]. Left party leader Luigi Pantisano said such a law would not survive the Federal Constitutional Court [20] [21]. The Berlin Left decides on coalition talks at a party congress next Saturday [20].

Confidence is high on Dobrindt's quote and the Left's reaction, because tagesschau and DER SPIEGEL report them and the ministry confirmed the plan. Confidence is moderate on the draft's details, which rest on Bild's first report and have not been published as a bill.

items.title: Baden-Württemberg's Hagel Condemns Attacks on Police at Stuttgart Ulm 5 Rally
items.lede: The state interior minister also warned organisers of 31 October youth protests that masking up will not be tolerated, citing scenes from France.

sections.text: Several hundred people marched through central Stuttgart, Germany, on Saturday under the slogan 'Free the Ulm 5', backing pro-Palestinian activists jailed over an attack on the Ulm site of Israeli arms firm Elbit [22] [23]. Police counted 600 to 700 participants and organisers about 1,000 [22]; police reported arrests, pyrotechnics, masked marchers, and pepper spray use, and three officers were hurt, one unfit for duty [23]. The five defendants are on trial at Stuttgart regional court for property damage, trespass, and alleged membership of a criminal organisation [22]. On Sunday, state Interior Minister Manuel Hagel (CDU) told dpa that 'three injured police officers are three too many' and that police and prosecutors would identify the attackers [24]. Looking ahead to education protests planned in many German cities on 31 October, he said 'rioting is not youth protest' and 'the images from France are not a model', adding that security agencies also see calls for violent protest [24]. No arrest count was found by the cutoff.

Confidence is high on the march, the crowd estimates, the charges, and Hagel's remarks, because dpa and SWR report them citing police, the court, and the minister. Confidence is moderate on the clashes, which rest on police statements relayed by SWR.
